stem: A 64-year-old with stable angina took sildenafil last evening. He now has chest pain and reaches for his sublingual nitroglycerin. Why is this dangerous?
correct: Both raise cGMP: life-threatening hypotension

distractors.text: Sildenafil blocks nitrate absorption under the tongue
distractors.why: The interaction is additive vasodilation.

distractors.text: Both cause reflex bradycardia and AV block
distractors.why: That is the verapamil or diltiazem with beta-blocker risk.

distractors.text: Sildenafil causes nitrate tolerance within hours
distractors.why: Tolerance comes from continuous nitrate exposure.

distractors.text: Both constrict the afferent arteriole: kidney injury
distractors.why: That is the NSAID mechanism.

why_correct: Nitrates donate NO and raise cGMP; PDE5 inhibitors block cGMP breakdown. Together they cause life-threatening hypotension.
takeaway: Nitrate + PDE5 inhibitor: never.
discriminator: Make more cGMP + stop its breakdown.

stem: A 61-year-old on lisinopril for 3 months has a dry, nagging cough with clear lungs. A second patient on lisinopril arrives with lip and tongue swelling. Which pair of actions is correct?

stem: A 74-year-old takes losartan and furosemide. After a week of over-the-counter ibuprofen for knee pain, creatinine has doubled. Which explanation is most complete?
correct: Afferent constriction, efferent dilation and volume loss together

distractors.text: Ibuprofen alone is directly toxic to the renal tubules
distractors.why: The lecture's point is the three combined hemodynamic hits.

distractors.text: Losartan caused bradykinin build-up in the glomerulus
distractors.why: ARBs do not act through bradykinin.

distractors.text: Furosemide caused hyperkalemia that injured the kidney
distractors.why: Loops lower potassium.

distractors.text: Efferent constriction from ibuprofen raised filtration
distractors.why: NSAIDs constrict the afferent arteriole and filtration falls.

why_correct: NSAID (afferent constriction) + ACE inhibitor or ARB (efferent dilation) + diuretic (volume depletion): filtration pressure collapses. Common, often missed and preventable; ask about OTC NSAIDs.
takeaway: ACEi/ARB + diuretic + NSAID = AKI.
discriminator: Each drug alone is tolerated; the three together are not.

stem: A 69-year-old on lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide has had vomiting and diarrhea for 2 days and is light-headed on standing. She asks what to do with her medicines. Which advice fits?
correct: Hold the ACE inhibitor until she is eating and drinking again

distractors.text: Continue everything; missed doses cause rebound hypertension
distractors.why: Rebound is the clonidine warning.

distractors.text: Double the lisinopril to protect the kidney while ill
distractors.why: RAAS blockade plus low perfusion can cause AKI.

distractors.text: Add ibuprofen for the aches and keep all the others
distractors.why: That completes the triple whammy.

distractors.text: Stop lisinopril permanently and never restart it
distractors.why: It is held during the illness, not abandoned.

why_correct: Sick-day rules: hold the ACE inhibitor or ARB during vomiting, diarrhea or dehydration, because RAAS blockade with reduced renal perfusion can precipitate AKI.
takeaway: Vomiting or diarrhea: pause the ACE inhibitor or ARB.
discriminator: Temporary hold vs permanent stop.

discriminator: Vessel-selective vs heart-slowing CCBs.

stem: A 70-year-old with CKD (GFR 24) has worsening leg edema and blood pressure 162/94 on hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, lisinopril and amlodipine. He takes all three reliably. Which change is most likely to help?

distractors.why: Thiazides fade below a GFR of about 30.

distractors.text: Add clonidine as a fourth antihypertensive class
distractors.why: The problem is an ineffective diuretic, not a missing class.

distractors.text: Add hydralazine alone for its arteriolar dilation

distractors.why: Nothing here says the ACE inhibitor is the problem.

discriminator: A new class vs fixing the diuretic you already have.

stem: An 84-year-old with CKD is admitted with a serious infection and needs a renally cleared antibiotic. Her creatinine clearance is markedly reduced. Which dosing approach matches the lecture?
correct: Usual loading dose, then a reduced maintenance dose

distractors.text: Reduced loading dose, then the usual maintenance dose
distractors.why: Loading is often unchanged; maintenance is what is adjusted.

distractors.text: Usual loading and usual maintenance, with levels if toxic
distractors.why: A renally cleared drug accumulates when GFR is low.

distractors.text: No loading dose, then double the interval and the dose
distractors.why: Skipping the load delays effect; doubling the dose defeats the cut.

distractors.text: Avoid every renally cleared drug in any patient with CKD
distractors.why: The drugs are adjusted, not banned.

why_correct: As GFR falls, renally cleared drugs accumulate. Check creatinine clearance, then lower the maintenance dose, extend the interval, or both. Loading doses are often unchanged.
takeaway: Low GFR: keep the load, cut the maintenance.
discriminator: Loading fills the volume; maintenance replaces what is cleared.
